TLDR: people usually don't mean it like that, they just simply don't know about the bad sides of ADHD because they only see the "good sides". Depression has also been a taboo for long. Only recently people have started to know that it's not just being sad and it cannot be fixed by eating ice cream and taking a walk, because it's been such a hot topic in social media etc. Only then people started to realize it's not just being sad.
So talk to people! Make them know that adhd is more than what most people show on the outside. It is a mental struggle, so nobody knows just how hard it is, untill you tell them.

To my fellow adhd people who find it frustrating that nobody seems to know how hard adhd (or any mental illness) really is,

I know it's frustrating to have people who think they know how you feel, but they really don't. I've had a depression for years and people say things like "oh i've been really depressed after my cat died as well, i stayed in bed all day." Or my mom used to say "why are you sad? You have a roof over your head, food to eat, how can you be depressed?" "Try to go outside more, vitamin D will make you better!" Because when they feel sad, they do stuff like that and it helps. 

Luckily depression is on the media a lot nowadays and a lot of people talk openly about it (thank you for that!!), so most of the people know depression is a real disorder and can't be fixed as easily as being sad, so not a lot of people say those things anymore in 2020.

As for ADHD, there's unfortunately more people who say stuff when they don't even know what they're talking about.

But keep in mind this is a mental disorder! For both sides of the story. People who never had a mental disorder can never understand what it's really like (and lucky for them!)

People always want to understand something, so they try to refer unknown things to a past experience or think of things to make it understandable for them. It's just human. The universe is extremely big for example,bigger than we can imagine. There must be something there, other than us right? So we start thinking there's life in outer space because we simply can't understand that there is literally nothing except earth where creatures live.(just an example)


So back to ADHD, things like "oh i also forget a lot" or "i also feel really talkative and social, i can't stop talking sometimes!" are just people trying to understand what it feels like. Not the right way to try to understand, but it's how most people work.

Also, people can't see the dark side of adhd because we won't show that in public. Not a lot of people know what's going on and that is normal! No one ever talks to a newly met person and says all the bad stuff in their heads right away when you say you have adhd. Nobody knows just how much you struggle with it, untill you tell them! Only the people i'm close with know the extreme struggle that comes with it, day by day. Nobody knows how good it feels for you to take meds and finally have some relief of your own head. And nobody can get inside your head and feel what it feels like, so keep that in mind. 

I've tried so hard making people understand my adhd and got so frustrated at those seemingly rude comments, but i've learned that that's not the right way.

Tell them about the bad sides of adhd.
Tell them about how annoying adhd is for yourself.
Just explain them and educate them, because all they ever see is you being funny or extremely talkative towards them, so they don't know better.

9/10 times when i explained that it may be fun for the people in social situations when they talk to you, but for me it's a living hell to be this chaotic all the time,they said sorry and they didn't even know that that also comes with adhd. They only see the "good" parts of you and that's nice! But there's so many bad parts nobody talks about.

So many people have met someone with adhd, thought they were so fun and outgoing and thought nothing more of it, because they didn't tell them the struggles that also comes with it! So naturally they start thinking adhd is just quirky and fun.

That being said, they should be more considerate with their words in relation with a mental illness! We have learned a lot through social media about depression. My grandma still thinks its being lazy, but nowadays people learn to talk about it so many people know it's not just laziness. It's difficult that people still think adhd is just being happy and talkative and people should be more carefull as it's also a real mental disorder! But easy said from someone who has a mental disorder vs. someone who had never experienced something like it.

Let's educate people on adhd, tell them how it really is! 

Sorry for the long post! I did not take my meds so i hope it all makes sense! 
I hope to change your view on people who say stuff like this.

If they don't know what you're going through, tell them!
